subject: ela
intro: Seventh graders write routinely over extended time frames (time for research, reflection, and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of tasks, purposes, and audiences. Some writing, like a research paper, takes time; other writing, like a quick response or journal entry, is done in one sitting.

items.prompt: Which task needs an EXTENDED time frame: a research report or a quick journal entry?

steps: A research report needs time for research, drafting, and revision.
So the research report needs an extended time frame.

items.prompt: Why is REFLECTION and revision time important for longer projects?

steps: Time lets you rethink, gather more evidence, and improve the draft.
So reflection and revision make longer writing stronger.
solution.answer: It lets you improve ideas, gather evidence, and strengthen the draft.

items.prompt: Give an example of SHORT time-frame writing.

steps: Short writing is done in one sitting.
So a journal entry, a quick answer, or a short response.
solution.answer: A journal entry or a quick written response.

items.prompt: A research paper needs an ____ time frame.
A journal entry is a ____ time-frame task.
Writing often should become a ____ habit.
